criteria.description: Specifies how feature quality will be measured before/after ship — e.g. a golden/test set, a rubric, offline and/or online quality signals. A vague 'we'll monitor it' does not count.
Defines what the user experiences when the model is low-confidence, out of scope, or fails — and it is not just a generic error message or a dead end.
Enumerates AI-specific failure modes (e.g. hallucinated/incorrect action items, missed items, wrong owner/date) and pairs each with a detection or mitigation.
Questions or justifies why AI is the right approach versus a simpler/deterministic baseline.
Addresses confidence/legibility and lets the user verify, edit, or undo the AI output (human-in-the-loop), rather than treating output as final.
Treats cost and/or latency as an explicit product constraint with a target or budget, not an afterthought.
Success metrics span more than one dimension — e.g. at least a quality measure plus an adoption/outcome measure, ideally with a guardrail metric that must not regress.
Proposes a staged rollout (e.g. shadow/canary/GA) with a gate or kill switch, rather than a single launch.
